q: 设计原则和 OOP 概念在 LLD 里各自负责什么？
q_en: In low-level design, what job does each of design principles and OOP concepts do?
options: 两者是互不相关的两套独立知识
OOP 概念只在系统设计面试才会考，LLD 白板题只考数据结构和算法
设计原则决定取舍方向，OOP 概念是实现这些取舍的语言机制
设计原则的内容只适用于前端框架代码
options_en: The two pages are unrelated, independent topics.
OOP concepts are only tested in system-design interviews — LLD whiteboard rounds only test data structures and algorithms.
Design principles decide the direction of a tradeoff, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that implement it.
Design principles only apply to frontend framework code.
why: 设计原则回答“该怎么取舍”，封装、抽象、多态、继承回答“怎么把取舍写进类和接口里”。两者是同一决策链的上下游。
why_en: Design principles decide what tradeoff to make, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that turn that tradeoff into classes and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

optionExplanations: 把两者当成孤立知识会让你在面试里各说各话；实际上原则给方向，OOP 概念给落地方式。
LLD 白板题不只考数据结构和算法，还要求把取舍落成类和接口，OOP 概念天天用到。
对：原则先定取舍方向，接口、封装、继承再把这个方向落成具体代码结构。
设计原则同样适用于后端类设计，把它限定在前端框架是范围搞错了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating them as unrelated leaves you unable to connect tradeoffs to code in an interview — principles set direction, OOP concepts implement it.
LLD whiteboard rounds test more than data structures and algorithms — they require turning tradeoffs into classes and interfaces, where OOP concepts show up constantly.
Correct: principles set the tradeoff direction first, then encapsulation, interfaces, and inheritance turn that into class structure.
Design principles apply just as much to backend class design, not only frontend framework code.
scenario: LLD 面试设计支付网关：先定下"新增支付渠道不改旧代码"，接着要落成具体的类与接口。
scenario_en: In an LLD interview for a payment gateway, you first settle on "adding a new channel must not touch old code", then you have to turn that into actual classes and interfaces.

q: 补全四个核心 OOP 概念：
q_en: Fill in the four core OOP concepts:
text: LLD 面试中最重要的四个 OOP 概念是：{{封装}}、{{抽象}}、{{多态}}、{{继承}}。
why: 不需要死背术语，但要能在类设计里自然应用它们。
why_en: The four core OOP concepts are encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

q: 封装的核心含义是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of encapsulation?
options: 隐藏对象内部数据，通过方法控制访问和修改
把所有字段都设为 public，方便外部直接读写
让每个类都必须继承一个公共父类
只写静态函数，不定义任何实例方法
options_en: Hide an object's internal data and control access and changes through methods.
Make every field public so external code can read and write it directly.
Force every class to inherit from a common parent class.
Write only static functions and define no instance methods.
why: 封装让对象自己维护规则，例如余额不能为负、停车位不能被外部随意改。调用方通过行为而不是直接改字段来交互。
why_en: Encapsulation hides internal data and exposes controlled behavior so the object itself can enforce its own rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

optionExplanations: 对：把状态藏起来、只开放受控方法，是封装的核心动作。
全部字段设为 public 正好是封装要防止的做法，外部能绕开校验直接改状态。
强制继承公共父类说的是继承而不是封装，两个概念被混在一起了。
只写静态函数会让对象没有自己的状态可藏，根本谈不上封装。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: hiding internal data and only allowing controlled methods to touch it is exactly what encapsulation does.
Making every field public is the exact failure mode encapsulation prevents — callers can bypass validation.
Forcing every class to inherit a common parent describes inheritance, not encapsulation — a different concept.
Static-only functions leave no instance state to hide, so there's nothing to encapsulate.
scenario: 银行账户类要求余额永不为负，而调用方分散在转账、结算、对账三处代码里。
scenario_en: A bank account class must guarantee the balance never goes negative, but callers live in three different places: transfer, settlement, and reconciliation.

scenario: ParkingLot 暴露 public spots: list[ParkingSpot]，任何调用方都能直接增删停车位。
scenario_en: ParkingLot exposes a public spots: list[ParkingSpot] field, so any caller can add or remove parking spots directly.
q: 主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem here?
options: 列表本身不能用来存对象，得换成字典
外部代码可以绕过 ParkingLot 的规则，直接增删内部车位列表
每个 ParkingSpot 都必须实现成 Singleton 才安全
问题在于 Python 语言本身不支持 private 约定
options_en: Lists simply cannot hold objects, so it must become a dict.
External code can bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate the internal spot list directly.
Every ParkingSpot must be implemented as a Singleton to be safe.
The real problem is that Python has no private-field convention.
why: 公开可变集合会让调用方绕过 park_vehicle 等受控方法直接改内部状态，破坏不变量。应提供受控方法并返回副本或只读视图。
why_en: Exposing a mutable internal collection lets callers bypass ParkingLot's rules and mutate its internal state directly, breaking its invariants.
whenOtherWins: 只读 DTO 或测试夹具可以直接暴露简单字段，但核心领域对象应保护可变状态。
tradeoff: 私有集合 + 受控方法 vs 公开可变集合：前者安全但多一层方法调用，后者简单但任何人都能破坏不变量。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton：一种保证某个类全局只有一个实例的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Singleton is a design pattern that guarantees a class has only one instance across the whole program.

termDefinitions.meaning: private：一种把字段/方法标记为只能在类内部访问的可见性约定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Private is a visibility convention that marks a field or method as accessible only from inside its own class.

optionExplanations: 列表完全可以存对象，问题不在数据结构类型，是暴露方式本身。
对：公开可变列表让外部绕开 park_vehicle 直接改车位，破坏了内部不变量。
车位对象要不要唯一实例和这里的问题无关，Singleton 解决的是另一件事。
Python 用下划线前缀和 @property 就能表达受保护/私有，语言并不缺这个能力。
optionExplanations_en: Lists can absolutely hold objects — the real issue is exposure, not the data structure choice.
Correct: a public mutable list lets callers skip park_vehicle and mutate spots directly, breaking invariants.
Whether a spot needs a single instance is unrelated here — Singleton solves a different problem.
Python expresses private/protected fine via underscore prefixes and @property; the language isn't missing this.

scenario: 调用方需要查看停车位列表，但不应能修改 ParkingLot 内部列表。
scenario_en: A caller needs to view the parking spot list, but must not be able to modify ParkingLot's internal list.
q: 这段 getter 的关键目的是什么？
q_en: What is the key purpose of this getter?
options: 让外部更容易删除内部元素
把 ParkingLot 变成不可实例化的类
自动给每次调用加锁
返回列表的副本，避免外部直接改动内部集合
options_en: Make it easier for external code to delete internal elements.
Turn ParkingLot into a class that can never be instantiated.
Automatically lock every call to this property.
Return a copy of the list so external code can't mutate the internal collection.
why: @property 返回 list(self._spots) 的副本，调用方可以读取结果，但无法通过引用篡改内部状态。
why_en: Returning a copy of the list preserves encapsulation because callers can read the result but cannot mutate the internal state through a shared reference.
whenOtherWins: 如果集合很大，复制成本高，可能改用只读视图、迭代器或查询方法代替整体复制。
tradeoff: 返回副本 vs 返回内部引用：副本安全但有复制开销，直接返回引用零开销但会泄漏可变状态。

termDefinitions.meaning: getter：用于读取对象内部字段的只读访问方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A getter is a method that provides read-only access to an object's internal field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

optionExplanations: getter 返回的是副本，删除副本里的元素不会影响内部列表，达不到这个效果。
@property 只是暴露一个只读视图，跟类能不能被实例化没有关系。
这段代码没有任何加锁逻辑，getter 只是做了复制，不涉及并发控制。
对：这个 property 每次调用都产出一份新拷贝，调用方拿到的只是快照，动不了内部集合本身。
optionExplanations_en: The getter returns a copy, so deleting from that copy never touches the internal list — this doesn't happen.
The @property just exposes a read-only view; it has nothing to do with whether the class can be instantiated.
There's no locking here at all — the getter is just a copy, not a concurrency mechanism.
Correct: this property produces a fresh copy on every call, so the caller only ever holds a snapshot, never the internal collection itself.

q: 抽象的核心含义是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of abstraction?
options: 暴露必要能力，隐藏实现细节
把所有内部字段都暴露给调用方
让每个类都改写成公共父类
只使用全局函数，不定义接口
options_en: Expose only the essential capability and hide the implementation details.
Expose all internal fields to every caller.
Rewrite every class to be a shared parent class.
Use only global functions and never define an interface.
why: 抽象定义“能做什么”，不泄露“怎么做”。调用方依赖清晰接口，具体实现可以替换。
why_en: Abstraction exposes essential capabilities while hiding implementation details behind a clear contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接口（Interface）：只声明方法契约、不含实现，供多个类各自实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface declares a method contract with no implementation, which multiple classes can implement independently.

optionExplanations: 对：只给调用方需要的能力契约，具体怎么实现留在类内部。
全部字段暴露出去正是抽象要避免的，调用方会直接依赖内部实现。
让每个类共享一个父类说的是继承的做法，跟隐藏实现细节没关系。
只用全局函数反而丢掉了契约的边界，没有接口就没法约束调用方依赖什么。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: expose only the capability contract the caller needs, and keep the how inside the class.
Exposing every internal field is exactly what abstraction avoids — callers end up depending on internals.
Sharing one parent class across every type describes inheritance, not hiding implementation.
Global-only functions actually remove the contract boundary — no interface means nothing constrains what callers depend on.
scenario: 支付服务今天走 Stripe，半年后可能换 Adyen，上游下单代码不想跟着一起改。
scenario_en: The payment service runs on Stripe today and may switch to Adyen in six months, and the upstream checkout code must not have to change with it.

scenario: OrderService 直接调用 StripeAPI.set_api_key() 和 create_charge()，以后换 PayPal 要改 OrderService。
scenario_en: OrderService calls StripeAPI.set_api_key() and create_charge() directly, so switching to PayPal later would require changing OrderService.
q: 更好的抽象是什么？
q_en: What would be a better abstraction here?
options: 让 OrderService 直接继承 StripeAPI 类
把 StripeAPI 实例设为 OrderService 的 public 字段
定义 PaymentMethod 接口，只暴露 process(amount) 方法
把支付调用逻辑整体搬到前端 UI 层去写
options_en: Have OrderService directly inherit from the StripeAPI class.
Make the StripeAPI instance a public field on OrderService.
Define a PaymentMethod interface that only exposes process(amount).
Move all payment logic into the frontend UI layer.
why: 订单服务只需要“处理支付”这个能力，不该绑定 Stripe 的具体 API 细节。接口让支付实现可替换。
why_en: A PaymentMethod abstraction lets OrderService depend on the ability to process a payment instead of Stripe-specific details.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统永远只用一个支付实现且代码很小，直接调用可能符合 KISS。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 接口 vs 直接调用 StripeAPI：接口多一层抽象但换供应商不用改 OrderService；直接调用更省事但换 PayPal 要重写调用方。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中负责结账流程的订单服务类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OrderService is the class in this example responsible for the checkout flow.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方支付服务商 Stripe 的具体 API 客户端类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: StripeAPI is the concrete client class for the third-party payment provider Stripe.

termDefinitions.meaning: PaymentMethod：本例中定义“处理支付”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentMethod is the interface in this example that defines the capability to process a payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS：保持设计足够简单、不要过度设计的原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, and it means don't over-engineer a design.

diagram:
classDiagram
  class OrderService
  class PaymentProcessor {
    +process(amount)
  }
  class StripeProcessor
  class PayPalProcessor
  OrderService --> PaymentProcessor
  PaymentProcessor <|.. StripeProcessor
  PaymentProcessor <|.. PayPalProcessor
optionExplanations: 继承会把 OrderService 和 Stripe 的具体实现焊死在一起，换供应商时要动订单服务本身。
public 字段等于把 Stripe 细节直接摊开给调用方，谁都能绕开抽象直接摆弄 Stripe 对象。
对：接口只留 process(amount) 一个方法，OrderService 不用关心背后是 Stripe 还是别的供应商。
支付涉及密钥和金额校验，搬到前端等于把敏感逻辑暴露给客户端，安全上不可行。
optionExplanations_en: Inheriting from StripeAPI welds OrderService to Stripe's concrete implementation, so switching providers means editing OrderService itself.
A public field just hands Stripe's details straight to callers, letting anyone bypass the abstraction and poke at the Stripe object.
Correct: the interface only exposes process(amount), so OrderService never needs to know whether it's Stripe or another provider.
Payment involves secret keys and amount validation — moving it to the frontend exposes sensitive logic to the client, which isn't safe.

q: 好的抽象层级应该围绕什么设计？
q_en: What should a good abstraction level be designed around?
options: 把接口做到越泛越好，比如只留一个 doWork()
围绕调用方真正需要执行的业务操作来设计
把内部实现的每个小步骤都单独暴露出来
把接口做到越具体越好，比如 callStripeCreateChargeOnly()
options_en: Make the interface as generic as possible, like a single doWork().
Design it around the actual operation the caller needs to perform.
Expose every small internal implementation step separately.
Make the interface as specific as possible, like callStripeCreateChargeOnly().
why: 接口太泛没有语义，太细又泄露实现。合适的抽象层级来自调用方的业务需要，而不是实现的步骤数。
why_en: A good abstraction is shaped around what the caller needs to do, not how many internal steps the implementation happens to have.
tradeoff: 过泛接口 vs 过细接口：doWork() 太泛让实现自己猜意图，callStripeCreateChargeOnly() 太细则泄漏了具体供应商，两者都不是调用方真正需要的契约。

termDefinitions.meaning: doWork(request)：一个只有动词、没有业务语义的过泛接口方法名示例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: doWork(request) is an example of an overly generic method signature that carries no real business meaning.

optionExplanations: doWork() 这种万能接口只在真的通用到没有业务语义时才有意义，多数场景下它把猜意图的负担甩给了实现者。
对：接口方法名对应调用方真正要做的业务动作，比如 processPayment(amount)，层级不多不少。
把内部每一步都单独暴露，调用方要自己拼装步骤顺序，这其实是把实现细节泄露成了接口。
callStripeCreateChargeOnly() 把供应商名字焊进了方法签名，换一家支付商就得改调用方代码。
optionExplanations_en: A catch-all doWork() only makes sense when the operation is truly generic; in most cases it just pushes the guessing of intent onto the implementation.
Correct: the interface names the actual business operation the caller performs, like processPayment(amount) — not too broad, not too granular.
Exposing every internal step forces the caller to assemble the sequence itself, which leaks implementation detail into the interface.
callStripeCreateChargeOnly() bakes the vendor name into the method signature, so switching payment providers forces callers to change too.
scenario: 订单服务要调支付网关：接口既要能换供应商，又要让调用方一眼看懂它在做什么业务。
scenario_en: The order service calls a payment gateway: the interface has to survive swapping vendors and still make it obvious to the caller what business action it performs.

q: 多态在 LLD 中通常用来替代什么？
q_en: What does polymorphism usually replace in LLD?
options: 所有对象初始化时执行的构造函数逻辑
所有字段声明时使用的默认初始值
所有异常捕获与错误处理相关代码
根据对象类型走不同分支的判断逻辑
options_en: Every constructor's logic for initializing a new object.
The default initial value assigned to every declared field.
All exception-catching and error-handling related code.
Branching logic that dispatches based on an object's type.
why: 当行为随类型变化时，让每个对象实现同一接口并自己处理，比到处写 type 判断更可扩展。
why_en: Polymorphism replaces type-checking branches by letting each implementation handle the same operation in its own way.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[type switch] --> B{vehicle type}
  B --> C[car logic]
  B --> D[bike logic]
  B --> E[truck logic]
  F[Vehicle.park] --> G[object decides]
optionExplanations: 构造函数负责初始化对象，跟“同一方法不同实现”这件事没有直接关系。
字段默认值是初始化数据，多态解决的是行为分派，不是给字段赋初值。
异常处理是错误路径的机制，跟按类型选择行为的问题不是一回事。
对：多态让每个类型自己实现同一方法，取代到处写 if vehicle.type == 'car' 这种判断。
optionExplanations_en: Constructors handle object initialization, which isn't the same problem as dispatching behavior by type.
Default field values are just initialization data — polymorphism is about dispatching behavior, not defaulting fields.
Exception handling is an error-path mechanism, a different concern from choosing behavior by type.
Correct: polymorphism lets each type implement the same method, replacing scattered if vehicle.type == 'car' checks.
scenario: 停车场要支持轿车/摩托/卡车，收费规则各不相同，下季度还会再加新车型。
scenario_en: A parking lot must handle cars, motorcycles and trucks with different fee rules, and more vehicle types are coming next quarter.

scenario: ParkingLot.park_vehicle() 根据 vehicle.type 判断 car、motorcycle、truck，分支越来越多。
scenario_en: ParkingLot.park_vehicle() branches on vehicle.type to handle car, motorcycle, and truck, and the branches keep growing.
q: 多态式改法是什么？
q_en: What is the polymorphic way to fix this?
options: 给 Vehicle 加统一的取尺寸方法，让子类各自返回自己的答案
继续在 if/elif 分支里不断添加新的车辆类型判断逻辑
让 ParkingLot 自己读取车辆的每个字段、自行猜测车辆类型是什么
干脆把所有车辆类型都统一当成 car 来处理，不做任何区分对待
options_en: Add a shared spot-size method to Vehicle and let each subclass return its own answer.
Keep adding more if/elif branches for each new vehicle type, without bound.
Have ParkingLot read every field itself and guess what the vehicle type actually is.
Just treat every vehicle the same way as a car, with no distinction at all.
why: 车辆知道自己需要什么车位，ParkingLot 只调用统一方法。新增车辆类型时尽量不改 ParkingLot。

optionExplanations: 多态确实多一次虚方法查找，但这点开销在大多数业务系统里完全不是瓶颈。

q: 继承最主要的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of inheritance?
options: 继承完全无法共享任何实现代码
继承只能用来实现接口，不能共享代码
父类的变化可能破坏所有子类，形成紧耦合
使用继承会自动提升代码的可维护性
options_en: Inheritance can never share any implementation code at all.
Inheritance can only be used to implement interfaces, never to share code.
A change in the parent class can break every subclass, creating tight coupling.
Using inheritance automatically improves maintainability.
why: 子类继承父类字段和方法，父类内部变化会影响整棵层次。这就是“脆弱基类”问题。
why_en: Inheritance tightly couples subclasses to the base class's implementation, so a base-class change can break the whole hierarchy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 脆弱基类问题：父类实现的一次改动，意外破坏了多个子类行为的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The fragile base class problem is when a single change to the parent implementation unexpectedly breaks multiple subclasses.

optionExplanations: 继承恰恰就是为了共享父类的字段和方法，说它完全不能共享代码正好说反了。
继承和实现接口是两件事，继承本身就是共享代码的手段之一。
对：子类紧耦合父类实现，父类一改，所有子类的行为都可能跟着变。
继承提高的是复用速度，不是可维护性，用不好反而会让改动牵一发动全身。
optionExplanations_en: Inheritance exists precisely to share a parent's fields and methods — saying it shares no code at all is backwards.
Inheriting and implementing an interface are different things; inheritance is itself one way to share code.
Correct: subclasses are tightly coupled to the parent's implementation, so one parent change can ripple through every subclass.
Inheritance speeds up reuse, not maintainability — used poorly it makes one change ripple through the whole hierarchy.
scenario: 支付基类被 6 个渠道子类继承，风控团队每个月都要改基类里的校验逻辑。

scenario: SavingsAccount 和 CheckingAccount 都确实共享余额、存款、取款和交易历史逻辑。

options: 共享的余额和交易逻辑稳定，两者都是 BankAccount 的特殊形式
只要两个类名字都带 Account 后缀、听起来相似，就足够构成继承的理由
因为组合这种设计手法根本没办法用来复用任何共享的实现代码
因为这两个子类打算把父类的所有行为逻辑完全推翻并重写一遍
options_en: The shared balance and transaction logic is stable, and both are genuine specializations of BankAccount.
Two classes merely sharing the Account suffix and sounding similar is already enough reason to reach for inheritance.
Composition as a technique simply has no way to reuse any shared implementation code at all.
The two subclasses intend to completely override and rewrite every single parent behavior.
why: 继承适合稳定、真实的 is-a 关系和共享实现。账户例子中核心余额行为一致，子类只是增加特定字段。
why_en: Inheritance fits when subclasses truly share stable implementation and are genuine specializations of the base class.
whenOtherWins: 如果差异主要是可替换的行为而非共享状态，组合接口通常更稳。
tradeoff: 继承 vs 组合：账户例子里核心逻辑稳定共享，继承省事；若账户类型未来行为差异很大，组合会更抗变化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的银行账户基类，持有余额并实现存取款逻辑。

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。

optionExplanations: 直接暴露可写字段等于放弃校验，任何调用方都能把余额改成负数或非法状态。
字段私有/受保护挡住了外部绕过方法直接改状态的路径，规则只能通过对象自己的方法生效。
只通过 deposit/withdraw 修改状态，把余额校验和记账逻辑锁在方法内部，杜绝跳过检查的写入。
返回副本或只读视图挡住了调用方通过引用篡改内部集合的可能，读没问题，写不到内部数据。
optionExplanations_en: Exposing a writable field directly means giving up validation — any caller can set balance to negative or invalid values.
Making fields private/protected blocks external code from bypassing methods to mutate state directly — rules only apply through the object's own methods.
Changing state only via deposit/withdraw locks balance validation and bookkeeping inside those methods, closing off writes that skip checks.
Returning a copy or read-only view blocks callers from mutating the internal collection through a shared reference — reads work, writes to internals don't.
scenario: 账户类要求余额永不为负，而且内部持仓列表不能被调用方在对象外偷偷改掉。
scenario_en: An account class must keep the balance non-negative, and its internal holdings list must not be mutated behind the object’s back.

q: 哪些信号说明可能需要抽象？（多选）
q_en: Which signals suggest you might need an abstraction? (multi-select)
options: 同一能力存在多个不同的实现
这块逻辑只有一个字段、并且以后也不会变化
某块逻辑里藏着很多变化的规则
调用方本不应该知道外部 API 的实现细节
options_en: The same capability has multiple different implementations.
This logic has only one field and it will never change.
A piece of logic hides a lot of varying rules.
Callers shouldn't need to know the implementation details of an external API.
why: 抽象适合隐藏复杂性和变化点。没有变化也不复杂的地方，抽象往往只是额外成本。
why_en: Abstraction helps when there are multiple implementations, complex variation, or details callers should not know about.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: API：应用程序编程接口，供调用方使用的一组预定义方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: API stands for Application Programming Interface, a predefined set of methods a caller can use.

optionExplanations: 同一能力有多个实现时，抽象挡住了调用方硬编码某一种实现的风险，换实现不用改调用方。
只有一个字段且永不变化，说明这里没有变化点要隐藏，硬加抽象反而多了一层没用的间接。
规则藏得越多，抽象把这些变化规则收进实现内部，调用方不用被每条规则牵连。
调用方不该知道外部 API 细节时，抽象挡住了供应商变更（如换支付商）传导到调用方代码的风险。
optionExplanations_en: When one capability has multiple implementations, abstraction blocks callers from hardcoding a specific one, so swapping implementations doesn't touch callers.
A single field that never changes has no variation to hide, so adding abstraction here is just an extra layer with no payoff.
The more varying rules hide inside a piece of logic, the more abstraction shields callers from being coupled to every one of those rules.
When callers shouldn't know external API details, abstraction blocks a vendor change (like switching payment providers) from rippling into caller code.
scenario: 订单系统里有一段通知逻辑，未来要支持短信、邮件、推送三种发送方式。
scenario_en: An order system has a notification step that will need to support SMS, email and push in the future.

scenario: 你看到 checkout 里根据 payment_type 字符串 switch 到不同支付逻辑。
scenario_en: You see checkout switch on a payment_type string to branch into different payment logic.
q: 这通常提示你使用什么概念？
q_en: What concept does this usually signal you should use?
options: 继承一个巨大的 PaymentProcessor 基类
把每种支付方式的字段都公开出来
定义 PaymentMethod 接口，让多态处理每种支付方式
在 checkout 里继续往 switch 加分支，新增支付方式还要跟着改这段代码
options_en: Inherit from one giant PaymentProcessor base class.
Expose every payment method's fields publicly.
Define a PaymentMethod interface and let polymorphism handle each payment type.
Keep adding branches to the switch inside checkout, so every new payment method means editing this same code again.
why: 支付方式是行为变化点。接口让每种支付自己实现 process，checkout 只调用统一方法。
why_en: A payment-type switch is a cue to use polymorphism through a shared PaymentMethod interface.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一种支付方式且没有扩展信号，先保持简单实现也可以。
tradeoff: PaymentMethod 多态 vs switch 分支：接口让新增支付方式不用改 checkout，但多定义一层接口；switch 写起来快，但每加一种支付都要回来改这段代码。

termDefinitions.meaning: PaymentMethod：本例中定义“处理支付”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentMethod is the interface in this example that defines the capability to process a payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中一个试图把所有支付方式塞进同一个继承体系的巨大基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PaymentProcessor here is a giant base class that tries to cram every payment method into one inheritance hierarchy.

optionExplanations: 继承一个巨大基类会把所有支付方式的字段和方法都塞进一棵层次，父类一改全体遭殃。
把字段全公开出来，调用方就要自己判断该用哪个字段，等于把分支判断从代码搬进了脑子里。
对：每种支付类型自己实现同一个 process 方法，checkout 端不用判断具体是哪种支付，直接调用即可。
继续往 switch 加分支，每新增一种支付方式都要回来改这同一段 checkout 代码。
optionExplanations_en: Inheriting one giant base class crams every payment method's fields and behavior into one hierarchy — a parent change hits everyone.
Exposing every field publicly just pushes the branching into the caller's head — it now has to know which fields apply to which method.
Correct: each payment type implements the same process method on its own, so checkout never has to branch — it just calls it.
Keep adding switch branches and every new payment method means editing this same checkout code again.

q: 用继承表达行为差异时，常见后果是什么？
q_en: What commonly happens when you use inheritance to express behavior differences?
options: 所有的变化都会自动变得更容易处理
子类会大量覆写父类方法，父类的契约变得脆弱
用继承之后就再也不需要接口了
只要用了继承，子类覆写父类的所有方法就自动被认为是正确的
options_en: Every future change automatically becomes easier to make.
Subclasses end up overriding many parent methods, and the parent's contract becomes fragile.
Once you use inheritance, you never need interfaces again.
Using inheritance automatically makes every method a subclass overrides correct.
why: 当子类只是为了不同实现而覆写父类方法，说明共享父类可能不是合适的抽象。组合可变行为通常更稳。
why_en: Using inheritance to express behavior variation often leads to many overrides and a fragile base-class contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

optionExplanations: 继承本身不会让变化自动变简单，用来表达行为差异时反而经常让改动更难追踪。
对：子类为了不同行为不停覆写父类方法，父类原本承诺的契约慢慢就不成立了。
继承和接口解决的是不同问题，用了继承之后该定义的契约接口通常还是要有。
继承只是复用了字段和方法，方法本身对不对跟有没有用继承没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: Inheritance doesn't automatically make change easier — using it to express behavior differences often makes changes harder to trace.
Correct: subclasses keep overriding parent methods for different behavior, and the parent's original contract gradually stops holding.
Inheritance and interfaces solve different problems — you typically still need a contract interface even after adding inheritance.
Inheritance just reuses fields and methods; whether a method is correct has no causal link to whether inheritance was used.
scenario: 为 5 种支付渠道建了统一 Payment 基类，结果每个子类都把 charge 和 refund 重写了一遍。
scenario_en: You built one shared Payment base class for five payment channels, and every subclass ended up overriding both charge and refund.

q: 把从 type-check 到多态停车的重构步骤排好：
q_en: Put the steps of refactoring from type-checks to polymorphic parking in the correct order:
steps: 为 Vehicle 定义所需车位尺寸契约
识别 switch/if 基于 vehicle.type 分支
为 Car/Motorcycle/Truck 实现各自尺寸
why: 先识别行为随类型变化，再把变化移进类型本身，最后调用方依赖统一契约。
why_en: Refactor type checks by identifying type-varying behavior, defining a contract, implementing it per type, and calling the contract.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中的停车场领域对象，管理车位集合与停车逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the domain object in this example that manages the collection of parking spots and the parking logic.

diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[type checks] --> B[define interface]
  B --> C[Car implements]
  B --> D[Motorcycle implements]

q: 把从错误继承到组合动力系统的步骤排好：
q_en: Put the steps of refactoring from broken inheritance to composed drivetrains in the correct order:
steps: Car 组合一个 Drivetrain 并委托 start
发现 ElectricCar 不共享 gasoline engine 行为
why: 先承认继承关系不稳定，再把可变行为抽出来组合。这样新增动力类型不会破坏 Car。
why_en: Move unstable behavior out of inheritance by defining a Drivetrain abstraction, implementing variants, and composing it into Car.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合（Composition）：一个类持有并委托给另一个对象，而不是继承它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition means a class holds a reference to another object and delegates to it instead of inheriting from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Drivetrain：本例中定义“启动动力系统”这一能力的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drivetrain is the interface in this example that defines the capability to start the car's power system.

scenario: 接口只有 doWork(request)，所有实现都要解析 request 内部并猜调用方意图。
scenario_en: An interface has only doWork(request), so every implementation must parse the request internals and guess the caller's intent.
q: 这可能是什么问题？
q_en: What is the likely problem here?
options: 问题在于这里的封装做得太强、外部什么状态和实现细节都完全看不到
问题在于这里定义的继承层次太少、类型分得太浅了
问题在于这种写法下多态机制根本不可能真正发生作用
接口太泛，doWork(request) 没表达出真实业务操作
options_en: The problem is that encapsulation here is too strong and no state or implementation detail is visible from outside at all.
The problem is that the inheritance hierarchy defined here has too few, too shallow levels.
The problem is that polymorphism can never actually kick in with this kind of shape.
The interface is too generic — doWork(request) never expresses the real business operation.
why: 接口名和参数应该表达调用方需要的业务能力。过泛接口会把复杂性转移给实现和读者。
why_en: An interface like doWork(request) is often too vague because it fails to express the real operation callers need.
whenOtherWins: 通用框架回调可能需要泛接口，但业务 LLD 中应优先清晰契约。
tradeoff: 泛接口 doWork(request) vs 具体方法名：泛接口看起来更通用，但每个实现都要重新解析意图；具体方法名（如 process(amount)）多写几个方法，但契约一看就懂。

termDefinitions.meaning: doWork(request)：一个只有动词、没有业务语义的过泛接口方法名示例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: doWork(request) is an example of an overly generic method signature that carries no real business meaning.

optionExplanations: 这里没有隐藏任何数据，doWork(request) 反而暴露太少语义，跟封装过强不是一回事。
这里根本没有继承关系，问题出在接口方法名，不是层次深浅。
多态照样能用在 doWork 上，各实现类各自处理 request，问题是接口没表达出业务意图。
对：doWork(request) 只是动词加参数，每个实现都得自己解析 request 猜调用方到底想干什么。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing is being hidden here — doWork(request) actually exposes too little meaning, which isn't the same problem as over-encapsulation.
There's no inheritance hierarchy involved at all — the issue is the interface's method name, not hierarchy depth.
Polymorphism still works fine on doWork; each implementation can handle request its own way — the real gap is the interface lacking business meaning.
Correct: doWork(request) is just a verb plus a blob, so every implementation has to parse request and guess what the caller actually wants.

scenario: Account.balance 是 public，任何代码都能直接设置为负数。
scenario_en: Account.balance is public, so any code can set it directly to a negative number.
q: 封装式修复是什么？
q_en: What is the encapsulation-based fix here?
options: balance 私有化，靠 deposit/withdraw 方法校验并修改
让所有调用方都凭自觉记得不要把余额设置成负数就可以了
把 balance 这个字段换一个新名字就能彻底解决这个问题了
用继承的方式定义一个子类，把 balance 字段包一层隐藏起来、避免直接暴露给外部
options_en: Make balance private and change it only through deposit/withdraw, which validate it.
Rely on every caller's self-discipline to remember never to set a negative balance.
Just rename the balance field to something new and that fully solves the problem.
Define a subclass through inheritance to wrap and hide the balance field so it's never directly exposed.
why: Account 拥有余额规则，就应在自己的方法里防止非法状态。依赖调用方自律不是可靠设计。
why_en: Make balance private and update it only through methods so Account itself can enforce valid balance rules.
whenOtherWins: 只读数据传输对象可以简单暴露字段，但有业务不变量的对象不应这样做。
tradeoff: 私有 balance + 方法校验 vs 公开字段：前者多写 deposit/withdraw 两个方法，但杜绝非法状态；后者零封装成本，但任何调用方都能把余额写成负数。

termDefinitions.meaning: 本例中持有余额并需要保证余额合法的账户对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Account is the object in this example that holds the balance and must keep it in a valid state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

optionExplanations: 对：balance 私有后只能靠 deposit/withdraw 改，方法里加校验就能直接拒绝非法值。
指望所有调用方都自觉遵守规则不是设计，只要有一处忘记校验，负余额照样能写进去。
换个字段名字不会改变它是 public 可写的事实，外部照样能直接把它设成负数。
继承解决的是共享父类字段方法的问题，跟隐藏这一个字段的可见性没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: once balance is private, it can only change through deposit/withdraw, and those methods can reject invalid values directly.
Relying on every caller to remember the rule isn't a design at all — one missed check anywhere still lets a negative balance through.
Renaming the field doesn't change the fact that it's still public and writable — external code can still set it negative directly.
Inheritance is about sharing a parent's fields and methods — it has nothing to do with hiding one field's visibility.

q: 哪些“需求信号 → OOP 概念”匹配合理？（多选）
q_en: Which "requirement signal → OOP concept" pairings are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 需要保护对象状态 → 封装
多个实现共享同一能力 → 抽象/多态
只要类名听起来相似 → 就该继承
行为差异很多、经常变化 → 优先用组合接口
options_en: Need to protect an object's state → encapsulation.
Multiple implementations share one capability → abstraction/polymorphism.
Class names merely sound similar → inheritance.
Behavior varies a lot and changes often → prefer composition with an interface.
why: 继承需要真实稳定的 is-a 和共享实现，不是看到相似名词就使用。
why_en: Inheritance requires a real, stable is-a relationship and shared implementation, not just similar-sounding names.
whenOtherWins: 如果多个“相似名词”的类确实共享稳定实现且行为一致，继承仍然可能是对的选择。
tradeoff: 抽象/多态 vs 继承：前者只要求实现同一契约、各自变化；后者要求真正稳定共享的实现，否则父类一变就牵连所有子类。

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象（Abstraction）：只暴露调用方需要的能力契约，隐藏具体实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Abstraction means exposing only the capability contract a caller needs, while hiding implementation details.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组合（Composition）：一个类持有并委托给另一个对象，而不是继承它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition means a class holds a reference to another object and delegates to it instead of inheriting from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

optionExplanations: 对：需要保护状态时用封装挡住外部直接改字段的风险，规则只能靠对象自己的方法生效。
对：多个实现共享同一能力时，抽象/多态把“调用哪个方法”和“具体谁来执行”解耦开。
光凭类名相似就继承，挡不住任何风险，反而可能把本不该共享实现的两个类硬绑在一起。
对：行为差异大又常变时，组合接口把每次变化限制在一个实现类里，不会牵连调用方。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: when state needs protecting, encapsulation blocks external code from writing fields directly — rules only apply through the object's own methods.
Correct: when multiple implementations share one capability, abstraction/polymorphism decouples which method is called from who actually runs it.
Using inheritance just because names sound alike blocks nothing — it can weld together two classes that shouldn't share implementation at all.
Correct: when behavior varies a lot and changes often, composition with an interface confines each change to one implementation class, not the caller.
scenario: 电商下单模块：订单状态要防篡改、支付渠道要多实现、促销规则每季度都变。
scenario_en: An e-commerce checkout module: order state must be tamper-proof, payment channels need several implementations, and promotion rules change every quarter.

scenario: 你在面试中把字段私有化、定义了接口、去掉了类型分支，但当下没说出“封装”“多态”这些术语名字。
scenario_en: In an interview you make fields private, define an interface, and remove type-checking branches, but in the moment you can't say the words "encapsulation" or "polymorphism."
q: 这样的设计表现应该如何评价？
q_en: How should this design performance be judged?
options: 如果面试中忘记术语名字，就一定会失败
必须先把封装、抽象、多态、继承的定义背熟，才能开始设计
把概念正确应用到设计里，比记住术语名字更重要
只要说出术语名字，就可以代替写代码
options_en: If you forget a term's name in the interview, you're guaranteed to fail.
You must memorize the definitions of encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance before you can start designing.
Applying the concept correctly in your design matters more than reciting its name.
Naming the right term can substitute for actually writing the code.
why: 如果你能把字段私有化、定义接口、去掉类型分支、避免错误继承，即使不说术语，设计也已经体现了这些概念。
why_en: Applying the OOP concepts correctly in your design matters more than being able to recite their names.
tradeoff: 术语准确 vs 概念应用：面试官更在意你的类设计是否体现了封装/抽象/多态/继承，而不是你是否说得出这些词。

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装（Encapsulation）：隐藏对象内部数据，只通过方法暴露受控的修改方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means hiding an object's internal data and exposing only controlled methods to change it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多态（Polymorphism）：不同类型的对象对同一方法调用各自给出自己的实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same method call with their own implementation.

optionExplanations: 面试官看的是类设计本身，忘记一个术语名字不等于设计里没有体现这个概念。
背熟定义不是设计的前提，很多工程师边设计边应用这些概念，术语反而是事后总结出来的。
对：私有化字段、定义接口、去掉类型分支，这些动作本身就是在应用封装/抽象/多态，说不说术语不改变这一点。
说出术语名字只是贴标签，面试官要看到接口设计和类结构，光说不写代码通不过。
optionExplanations_en: Interviewers judge the class design itself — forgetting one term's name doesn't mean the concept isn't present in the design.
Memorizing definitions isn't a prerequisite — many engineers apply these concepts while designing, and only name them afterward.
Correct: privatizing fields, defining interfaces, and removing type branches are the concepts in action — naming them or not doesn't change that.
Naming a term is just a label; interviewers need to see the interface design and class structure, not just hear the word.

q: 补全 OOP 总结口诀：
q_en: Fill in the OOP summary mnemonic:
text: {{封装}}隐藏状态、暴露行为；{{抽象}}定义契约；{{多态}}让对象自己处理类型差异；{{继承}}只在稳定共享实现时使用。
why: 这正是文章结尾的应用导向总结。
why_en: Encapsulation hides state, abstraction defines contracts, polymorphism handles type variation, and inheritance is for stable shared implementation.

q: 封装和抽象的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between encapsulation and abstraction?
options: 封装规定只能用在接口上，抽象规定只能用在字段上，两者不能同时用在一个类里
封装保护对象内部状态；抽象隐藏实现细节、暴露能力契约
封装和抽象说到底其实都等价于继承
封装和抽象都要求把状态改成全局变量
options_en: Encapsulation only applies to interfaces and abstraction only applies to fields, so the two can never appear in the same class.
Encapsulation protects an object's internal state; abstraction hides implementation details and exposes a capability contract.
Encapsulation and abstraction are really just the same thing as inheritance.
Both encapsulation and abstraction require turning state into global variables.
why: 封装更关注对象边界和状态不变量，抽象更关注调用方依赖什么能力而不是具体实现。二者常一起出现但不是同一件事。
why_en: Encapsulation protects internal state, while abstraction exposes a capability contract and hides implementation details.
tradeoff: 封装 vs 抽象：封装管的是“谁能碰我的状态”，抽象管的是“调用方需要知道多少实现细节”——一个是边界问题，一个是契约问题。

q: 哪些信号说明继承可能是合理选择？（多选）

options: 子类确实是父类的稳定特例
多个子类共享相同且稳定的实现
子类不会破坏父类承诺
子类主要通过抛异常来拒绝父类方法
options_en: The subclass is genuinely a stable special case of the parent.
Multiple subclasses share the same, stable implementation.
The subclass never breaks the parent's promised contract.
The subclass mainly rejects inherited methods by throwing exceptions.
why: 继承需要稳定 is-a 和共享实现。靠抛异常拒绝父类方法通常说明违反了 LSP。
why_en: Inheritance is reasonable when subtypes are stable specializations, share real implementation, and preserve the base contract.
tradeoff: 合理继承 vs LSP 违反信号：真正稳定的 is-a + 共享实现值得继承；子类靠抛异常拒绝父类方法，说明它其实不是父类的合法替代品。

termDefinitions.meaning: 继承（Inheritance）：子类自动复用父类字段和方法，但与父类实现紧耦合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance lets a subclass automatically reuse a parent class's fields and methods, at the cost of tight coupling to the parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP：里氏替换原则，子类必须能替换父类使用而不破坏程序正确性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP is the Liskov Substitution Principle: a subclass must be usable wherever its parent class is expected, without breaking correctness.

optionExplanations: 对：子类是父类的稳定特例时，继承挡住了“为不相关类型硬凑共享实现”这种风险。
对：多个子类共享同一稳定实现时，继承挡住了重复写同一段逻辑的成本。
对：子类不破坏父类承诺，挡住了调用方拿到子类实例后行为却和预期不一致的风险。
子类靠抛异常拒绝父类方法，说明它根本替换不了父类，这正是继承不该用的信号，不是可以用的信号。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: when a subclass is a genuinely stable specialization, inheritance avoids forcing shared implementation onto unrelated types.
Correct: when multiple subclasses share the same stable implementation, inheritance avoids duplicating that logic across each one.
Correct: when a subclass never breaks the parent's promised contract, inheritance avoids callers getting a subtype instance that behaves unexpectedly.
A subclass rejecting inherited methods by throwing exceptions means it can't actually substitute for the parent — that's a signal against inheritance, not for it.

scenario: 设计一族类型时，纠结用 interface 还是 abstract class。
scenario_en: Designing a family of types, unsure whether to use an interface or an abstract class.
q: interface 和 abstract class 的核心区别与选型是？
q_en: What is the core difference between interface and abstract class, and how to choose?
options: interface=「能做什么」的能力契约、可多实现;abstract class=带共享状态/代码的基类、只能单继承
interface 可以持有实例字段、构造函数和共享实现，而 abstract class 反倒只能声明纯抽象方法而已
两者完全等价，随便用哪个都行，无非是关键字不同、选型上没有任何实际区别
abstract class 能被一个类多重继承，interface 每个类只能实现一个
options_en: interface = a "can-do" capability contract, multiply implementable; abstract class = a base with shared state/code, single inheritance only
An interface can hold instance fields, constructors and shared implementation, while an abstract class can merely declare pure abstract methods and nothing else
They are completely equivalent; use either, it is just a different keyword with no real difference in choice
An abstract class can be multiply inherited by one class, while an interface can only be implemented once
optionExplanations: 对：一个 PaymentGateway 可以同时实现 Serializable 和 Auditable，但基类只能挑一个。
记反了：实例字段和构造函数是抽象类独有的，经典 interface 连状态都存不下。
当成关键字之争，就答不出"这里为什么不能用 abstract"——多实现和共享状态是两种约束。
数量搞反了：Java/C# 里类只能继承一个，interface 反而可以实现任意多个。
optionExplanations_en: Right: one PaymentGateway can implement both Serializable and Auditable, but it only gets to pick a single base class.
Backwards: instance fields and constructors belong to the abstract class; a classic interface cannot even hold state.
Treating it as a keyword argument leaves you unable to answer "why not an abstract class here" — multiple implementation and shared state are two different constraints.
The counts are flipped: in Java/C# a class extends one base but can implement any number of interfaces.
why: interface 是能力契约：无实例状态、一个类可实现多个；abstract class 是共享基类：能带字段和具体方法，但只能继承一个。拿不准选 interface。
why_en: An interface is a capability contract with no instance state that a class can implement many of, while an abstract class carries shared fields and code but you only get one — when in doubt, take the interface.
tradeoff: interface(能力·多实现·解耦·无共享代码) vs abstract class(共享状态+代码·单继承·绑定一族)
whenOtherWins: 只有一族紧密相关的类确实共享字段和具体实现时，abstract class 才划算；Python 里两者都写成 abc.ABC，纯契约可用 typing.Protocol。
whenOtherWins_en: An abstract class only pays off when a tightly-related family genuinely shares fields and concrete code; in Python both are written as abc.ABC and a pure contract can just be typing.Protocol.

一族相关类共享状态/代码

termDefinitions.meaning: 不能被直接实例化的基类,可同时含具体方法(共享代码)+抽象方法(留给子类实现)+实例字段+构造函数。表达 is-a、承载一族紧密相关类的共享实现;一个类只能继承一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class is a base that cannot be instantiated directly; it may hold concrete methods (shared code) + abstract methods (for subclasses) + instance fields + constructors. It expresses is-a and carries shared implementation for a tightly-related family; a class can extend only one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 纯能力契约:声明「能做什么」而(经典上)不带实现和实例状态。表达 can-do/角色,一个类可实现多个,是解耦(面向接口编程/DIP)的载体。Java8+ 允许 default 方法但仍无实例状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface is a pure capability contract: it declares "what can be done" without (classically) implementation or instance state. It expresses can-do/role, a class can implement many, and it is the vehicle for decoupling (program-to-interface/DIP). Java 8+ allows default methods but still no instance state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象基类的典型用法:基类写好算法「骨架」(固定流程),把其中变化的步骤留成抽象方法交子类填。这正是 abstract class 相对 interface 的独有价值——共享骨架 + 局部可变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Template Method is the archetypal use of an abstract base: the base defines the algorithm skeleton (fixed flow) and leaves the varying steps as abstract methods for subclasses to fill. This is exactly the value an abstract class adds over an interface — shared skeleton + local variation.

codeSample:
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol

# abstract class：给一族类共享状态 name + 共享方法 describe（模板），只留 area 变化点
class Shape(ABC):
    def __init__(self, name): self.name = name    # 状态：interface 给不了
    @abstractmethod
    def area(self) -> float: ...                   # 变化点，子类填
    def describe(self):                            # 共享具体方法，子类白继承
        return f"{self.name}: {self.area():.2f}"

class Circle(Shape):
    def __init__(self, r): super().__init__("圆"); self.r = r
    def area(self): return 3.14159 * self.r ** 2
# Circle(2).describe() 直接用基类的，不用重写

# interface（能力）：不相关的类都能实现，一个类可身兼多能
class JsonSerializable(Protocol):
    def to_json(self) -> str: ...

def save(o: JsonSerializable): print(o.to_json())  # 依赖能力，不依赖具体类
# Circle 和 User（毫无亲缘）各自写个 to_json 就都能被 save

scenario: OrderService 已依赖 PaymentMethod 接口，但 checkout 里仍写着 stripe = StripeAPI()。单元测试跑一次就打一次 Stripe 真实网络。

q: PaymentMethod 的具体实现该由谁创建、在哪一步装配？
q_en: Who should create the concrete PaymentMethod, and at which step is it wired in?
options: OrderService 构造函数收一个 PaymentMethod 参数，由上层装配代码决定传哪个实现
在 OrderService 构造函数里 new CreditCardPayment()，调用方就不用操心具体实现了
在 checkout 里按 order 的支付类型分支 new 出对应的 PaymentMethod 实现
给 PaymentMethod 接口加一个静态工厂方法，内部返回当前默认的支付实现
options_en: Have OrderService take a PaymentMethod in its constructor and let the caller decide which implementation to pass
Construct CreditCardPayment inside the OrderService constructor so callers never have to think about the implementation
Branch on the order's payment type inside checkout and construct the matching PaymentMethod there
Add a static factory method on PaymentMethod that hands back the current default payment implementation
optionExplanations: 对：OrderService 只声明「我需要一个能 process 的东西」，测试直接传假实现，一行网络都不发。
只是把 new 挪了个位置：类型仍写死在 OrderService 里，测试还是拿不到替身。
分支 new 把类型判断又搬回来了，加一种支付方式就要改 checkout——正是接口想消掉的东西。
工厂方法在需要按配置集中选实现时有用，但这里默认值仍藏在接口内部，测试无法逐用例替换。
optionExplanations_en: Right: OrderService only declares "I need something that can process", so a test can pass a fake and send zero network traffic.
This just moves the new: the concrete type is still hard-coded inside OrderService and tests still cannot substitute anything.
Branching to construct brings the type check back, and each new payment method edits checkout — exactly what the interface was meant to remove.
A factory helps when one place picks the implementation from config, but the default stays hidden inside the interface and tests cannot swap per case.
why: 接口只做到「不依赖具体类」，构造注入才做到「不负责创建具体类」——装配责任上移到 main/容器。代价：多一个装配点要维护。
why_en: The interface only removes the dependency on a concrete class; constructor injection also removes the job of creating it, pushing wiring up to main or a container — at the cost of one more assembly point to maintain.
tradeoff: 构造注入(实现可替换·可测试·多一个装配点) vs 类内 new(调用方省事·实现写死·测试打真实网络)
whenOtherWins: 实现只有一种、且永远不需要在测试里替换时（比如内部 Clock 包一层就用系统时间），类内直接 new 更省事，不值得为它拉一条装配链路。
whenOtherWins_en: When there is only one implementation and you never need to swap it in tests — say a Clock wrapper that always uses system time — constructing it inline is simpler and not worth a wiring chain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象需要的协作者由外部（构造函数参数、setter 或容器）传进来，而不是自己 new 出来。目的是让实现可替换、可在测试里换成假对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dependency injection means an object receives its collaborators from outside — via constructor parameters, setters or a container — instead of constructing them itself, so implementations stay swappable and testable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序里唯一一处知道所有具体实现并把它们组装起来的地方，通常是 main 函数或启动配置；其余代码只见接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The composition root is the single place in a program — usually main or a startup config — that knows every concrete implementation and wires them together, while all other code sees only interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写在类或接口上的静态方法，负责根据参数或配置返回某个具体实现，调用方不直接 new。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A static factory method is a static method on a class or interface that returns a concrete implementation based on arguments or config, so callers never call new directly.

scenario: 停车场用 _find_spot_by_size(size: str) 找车位，尺寸靠 "regular"/"large" 字符串传。有人写成 "Large"，代码照常跑，只是永远找不到车位。
scenario_en: A parking lot looks up spots with _find_spot_by_size(size: str), passing "regular"/"large" strings. Someone types "Large", the code still runs, it just never finds a spot.
q: 尺寸契约怎么定义才能让写错的值提前暴露？
q_en: How should the size contract be defined so that a wrong value surfaces early?
options: 定义 SpotSize 枚举，方法签名收 SpotSize，写错的成员名在编译/加载期就报错
在方法开头校验字符串是否落在允许集合里，不在就抛异常并打日志记下来
把三个字符串抽成模块级常量 REGULAR/LARGE/MOTORCYCLE，让调用方引用常量而不是字面量
给每种尺寸各写一个方法：find_regular_spot()、find_large_spot()、find_motorcycle_spot()
options_en: Define a SpotSize enum and have the method take SpotSize, so a misspelled member fails at compile or import time
Validate at the top of the method that the string is in the allowed set, and throw plus log when it is not
Pull the three strings into module-level constants REGULAR/LARGE/MOTORCYCLE so callers reference constants, not literals
Write one method per size: find_regular_spot(), find_large_spot(), find_motorcycle_spot()
optionExplanations: 对：SpotSize.LARGE 写错就是未定义名字，取值集合和类型一起被固定下来。
值从外部 JSON/表单进来时这层校验必须有，但它只把静默失效换成运行期异常，仍要跑到才知道。
常量能消掉拼写漂移，类型却还是 str——别处随手传个裸字符串照样通过。
把取值变成方法名，加一种尺寸就要加一个方法和一处调用分支，扩展点全散开了。
optionExplanations_en: Right: misspelling SpotSize.LARGE is an undefined name, and the set of legal values is pinned down together with the type.
You do need this layer when values arrive from external JSON or a form, but it only turns silent no-ops into runtime exceptions — you still must execute the path.
Constants stop spelling drift, yet the type is still str, so any other call site can pass a bare string and sail through.
Turning values into method names means each new size adds a method and another call-site branch, scattering the extension point.
why: 字符串是开放集合，工具无从判断哪些值合法；枚举把合法值收成封闭类型，错误从运行期静默失效前移到编译/加载期。代价：跨进程边界仍要做一次字符串到枚举的转换与校验。
why_en: A string is an open set so no tool can tell which values are legal, while an enum closes that set into a type and moves the error from a silent runtime no-op to compile or import time — the cost is converting and validating strings back into the enum at every process boundary.
tradeoff: 枚举(封闭取值·类型检查·跨边界要转换) vs 字符串魔法值(随手可写·拼错静默失效)
whenOtherWins: 取值集合由外部数据源动态决定、编译期根本列不全时（如租户自定义标签），只能用字符串加运行期校验，枚举反而每加一个值都要改代码重新发布。
whenOtherWins_en: When the set of values is decided by an external data source and cannot be enumerated at compile time — tenant-defined labels, say — strings plus runtime validation are the only option, since an enum would force a code change and redeploy per value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一组固定的具名取值定义成一个类型，成员在编译或加载期就确定；传错名字是语法错误而不是运行期的错值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An enum defines a fixed set of named values as a type whose members are fixed at compile or import time, so a wrong name is a syntax error rather than a bad value at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接写在代码里的裸字面量（"large"、3）,含义靠约定而非类型表达,拼错或改动时没有任何检查兜住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A magic value is a bare literal written inline, like "large" or 3, whose meaning rests on convention rather than a type, so nothing catches a typo or a change.

codeSample:
from enum import Enum

class SpotSize(Enum):        # 合法取值就这三个，封闭集合
    REGULAR = "regular"
    MOTORCYCLE = "motorcycle"
    LARGE = "large"

class Truck(Vehicle):
    def get_required_spot_size(self) -> SpotSize:
        return SpotSize.LARGE       # 写成 SpotSize.Large 直接 AttributeError

def _find_spot_by_size(self, size: SpotSize): ...   # 签名挡住裸字符串
# 边界处再转回来：SpotSize(payload["size"]) —— 非法值抛 ValueError

scenario: ParkingLot 内部有 5 万个 ParkingSpot。运维面板每秒读一次 spots 属性只为数一下空位，而现有 getter 每次都 return list(self._spots)。
scenario_en: A ParkingLot holds 50,000 ParkingSpot objects. An ops dashboard reads the spots property once a second just to count free ones, and today's getter does return list(self._spots) every time.
q: 这个高频只读调用该返回副本还是只读视图？
q_en: For this high-frequency read-only call, should the getter return a copy or a read-only view?
options: 返回只读视图：包一层不可变包装，调用方改不动，也不用逐个复制元素
返回副本 list(self._spots)：调用方拿到的是一份与内部无关的独立快照
直接返回 self._spots 本体，并在文档里注明调用方不要修改这个列表
返回副本，同时把内部改成不可变列表，每次新增车位就重建整个集合
options_en: Return a read-only view: wrap it so callers cannot mutate it and no elements get copied
Return a copy via list(self._spots): the caller gets an independent snapshot detached from the internals
Return self._spots itself and document that callers must not modify the list
Return a copy and also make the internal list immutable, rebuilding the whole collection on every new spot
optionExplanations: 对：包装只拦写操作，读一次的成本从 5 万次引用拷贝降到一次包装。
调用方要在遍历期间不受内部增删干扰时它才值这个钱，这里只数个数，每秒白拷 5 万个引用。
文档拦不住手：调用方一个 spots.clear() 就把停车场清空，正是封装要防的越权写。
重建集合把成本从读路径挪到写路径，每停一辆车都要复制全表，比原方案更贵。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the wrapper only blocks writes, so a read drops from 50,000 reference copies to one wrap.
This is worth paying for when the caller must iterate undisturbed by internal changes, but here it only counts, wasting 50,000 reference copies a second.
Documentation cannot stop a hand: one spots.clear() from a caller empties the lot, which is exactly the unauthorized write encapsulation exists to block.
Rebuilding the collection moves the cost to the write path, copying the whole table on every parked car — more expensive than what you started with.
why: 两者都挡住外部写，区别在拷贝成本与快照语义：视图零拷贝但是活的，内部增删会被调用方看见。代价：视图要求语言/库提供不可变包装，且调用方边遍历边发生内部变更时可能出错。
why_en: Both block outside writes; the difference is copy cost versus snapshot semantics — a view copies nothing but stays live, so internal changes show through, and it needs the language to offer an immutable wrapper.
tradeoff: 只读视图(零拷贝·随内部变化而变) vs 防御性拷贝(独立快照·每次读 O(n) 拷贝)
whenOtherWins: 调用方要在遍历期间保证内容稳定、或把结果跨线程/跨请求持有时，副本的独立快照才安全；集合只有几十个元素时拷贝开销可忽略，副本写起来也更简单。
whenOtherWins_en: A copy wins when the caller needs the contents stable while iterating, or holds the result across threads or requests; and when the collection is only a few dozen elements the copy cost is noise and the code is simpler.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对原集合的一层包装：读操作透传到原集合，写操作直接报错。不复制元素，因此原集合变了视图也跟着变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unmodifiable view is a wrapper over the original collection that passes reads through and rejects writes; it copies no elements, so changes to the original show through the view.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回（或接收）集合时复制一份再交出去，调用方拿到的是独立快照，改它不影响对象内部状态；代价是每次 O(n) 拷贝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A defensive copy duplicates a collection before handing it out or storing it, so the caller holds an independent snapshot whose changes cannot touch the object's internal state — at an O(n) cost per call.
